features.heading: Everything you need to manage contracts

features.i0desc: Extract supported contract fields with optional AI, then review the exact source text and page before saving them.
features.i1desc: Keep PDF and DOCX agreements, versions, folders, tags, and searchable contract content in one self-hosted workspace.

features.i3desc: Assign owners, due dates, reminders, subtasks, and completion status to obligations and renewal follow-up.
features.i4desc: Find agreement content and review an auditable history of contract and obligation changes.

dd.2desc: Assign owners, deadlines, reminders, and completion evidence for the work that continues after signature.

os.heading: Your contracts. Your infrastructure.
os.subtitle: Aakd is fully open source under the AGPL License. Deploy on your own servers for complete data sovereignty — no vendor lock-in, no per-seat pricing, no compromises.
os.0desc: Docker or bare metal. Run Aakd on infrastructure you control with the services listed in our self-hosting guide.
os.1desc: Connect local LLMs or use OpenAI, Anthropic, or another provider with your own keys. Data handling follows the provider and deployment you choose.
os.2desc: Developed in public with inspectable source, transparent issues, and contribution-friendly documentation.

integrations.heading: Connects to the tools you already use

faq.heading: Frequently asked questions
faq.a0: Yes. Aakd is open source under the AGPL License. You can self-host it at no cost with unlimited users, contracts, and features. A hosted version is not currently available.
faq.a1: Deploy with Docker using the services described in our self-hosting guide. We provide documentation and community support. Your data stays on infrastructure you control.
faq.q2: Can I use my own AI models?
faq.a2: Aakd currently supports documented Anthropic, OpenAI, and Ollama configurations. Bring your own provider key or run a local Ollama server; verify each provider before relying on an AI workflow.
faq.q3: Is Aakd suitable for enterprise use?
faq.a3: Aakd includes organization roles, access controls, and audit logging. SSO/SAML, formal compliance certifications, and hosted enterprise support are not currently included.
faq.q4: How do I migrate from DocuSign or other tools?
faq.a4: Aakd includes import tools for DocuSign, PandaDoc and CSV-based migration. Complex migrations require your own review and operational planning.
faq.a5: The interface supports English, Arabic with RTL, French, German, and Spanish. Authoring and drafting are later-phase surfaces in the Phase 0 release.

faqNew.title: What is available — and what is not.
faqNew.subtitle: Aakd is in Phase 0. Public claims should stay as inspectable as the product.

0.question: Is Aakd open source and self-hostable?
0.answer: Yes. The core is licensed under AGPL-3.0 and can be deployed on your own infrastructure using the documented stack.

1.question: Does Aakd make autonomous legal decisions?
1.answer: No. AI features produce reviewable suggestions and cited answers. Humans retain authority over canonical facts, legal decisions and consequential actions.

2.question: Do I need an AI provider to use Aakd?
2.answer: No. Repository, manual metadata, approvals, obligations and signing flows can work without an AI key. AI-assisted features require a configured supported provider.

3.question: Is a managed Cloud service available?
3.answer: Not currently. Managed Cloud belongs to a later roadmap phase and depends on activation, customer, reliability and operational evidence.

4.question: Does Aakd include enterprise certifications and SSO?
4.answer: Not currently. Organization roles, scoped access and audit records exist, while SSO/SCIM, formal certifications and enterprise assurance remain later-phase controls.
